title: Orientation
tagline: A question is typed into a box. This is where the journey, the method and the map begin.
story: A question is typed into a box and starts a journey. It will be counted, cached, matched with knowledge, checked, routed through tools and agents, and judged on the way out. At every stop something breaks or forces a choice, and the best answer depends on dials that nobody has told you yet.
oneLiner: Learn how the guide plays, practise Dial-and-Defend on a gentle board, and read a dated map of what changed in 2025 and 2026 before you quote a spec.
youWillLearn: Trace one question through the journey and name the world where each failure is fixed
Use the level loop: brief, options, dials, failure modes, quiz, defend, flashcards and references
Answer with Dial-and-Defend: clarify, list options, pick and flip, failure modes, metrics and rollout
Rank four ways to ground an assistant (prompt, RAG, tools, fine-tuning) as constraints change
Read a dated freshness map of 2025 and 2026 changes before you quote a spec in an answer
Run a workshop with facilitator mode, and export and import progress

flashcards.front: What are the five moves of Dial-and-Defend?
flashcards.back: 1 Clarify the dials. 2 List the options, including the boring one. 3 Pick for the stated dials and say what flips it. 4 Name failure modes and detection. 5 Name metrics and rollout.

flashcards.front: Why ask about dials before naming a technology?
flashcards.back: The best option moves with corpus size, update rate, permissions, latency, risk and cost. Interviewers listen for the dial set first.

flashcards.front: What is a dial?
flashcards.back: A constraint you can change, such as scale or permission model, that moves which option wins.

flashcards.front: What is the "boring option" in step 2?
flashcards.back: The simplest approach that could work, such as pasting the content into a cached prompt. It is the baseline every other option must beat.

flashcards.front: What does a good flip condition sound like?
flashcards.back: It names a dial and a threshold: "If the corpus outgrows the window, or permissions become per user, I switch to RAG."

flashcards.front: What steps make up one problem level?
flashcards.back: Brief, options board, flip the dials, failure modes, quiz, defend it, flashcards and references.

flashcards.front: Where does the guide save your progress?
flashcards.back: In your browser's local storage on that computer. Export a file from the footer or the Progress page to back it up or move it.

flashcards.front: What happens to progress if you clear site data or switch browsers?
flashcards.back: It is lost unless you exported first. Import the file to merge with or replace existing progress.

flashcards.front: What does facilitator mode do?
flashcards.back: It reveals quiz answers and model answers with an Answer key badge, and includes them when you print a level. Keep it off on learners' screens.

flashcards.front: How do you flip and grade a flashcard from the keyboard?
flashcards.back: Space flips the card. Keys 1 to 4 grade it.

flashcards.front: When did OpenAI release the Responses API, and when did the Assistants API shut down?
flashcards.back: Responses on 2025-03-11. Assistants deprecation was announced 2025-08-26 and the API shut down on 2026-08-26.

flashcards.front: What changed for prompt caching with the GPT-5.6 family?
flashcards.back: Cache writes bill at 1.25x input, explicit breakpoints and `prompt_cache_options` appear, `prompt_cache_retention` is deprecated and `prompt_cache_key` is optional. Older models return 400 for the new fields.

flashcards.front: What changed in the MCP revision dated 2026-07-28?
flashcards.back: A stateless protocol (no `initialize`, no session id), multi round-trip requests, Tasks moved to an extension, and sampling, roots, logging and DCR deprecated.

flashcards.front: Which A2A versions matter, and which does Foundry serve by default?
flashcards.back: v1.0.0 (2026-03-12) and v1.0.1 (2026-05-28). With no version header or `a2a-version` query value, Foundry serves preview 0.3.

flashcards.front: When did Microsoft Agent Framework reach 1.0?
flashcards.back: Announced 2026-04-03 for .NET and Python. Stable: agents, graph workflows, orchestrations, MCP. Preview at GA: memory, DevUI, hosted agent integration, AG-UI and more.

flashcards.front: When did Agent 365 reach GA, and for whom?
flashcards.back: 2026-05-01, for the Commercial segment, licensed per user. At least one user needs a qualifying license.

flashcards.front: What ended on 2026-08-20 for Foundry hosted agents?
flashcards.back: Support for the initial-preview hosted agent backend. Existing deployments are not migrated automatically, so redeploy on the new model.

flashcards.front: Which dates should you pin before the end of 2026?
flashcards.back: 2026-10-23 OpenAI model shutdowns, 2026-11-19 Azure o-series retirements, 2026-11-30 Evals and prompts shutdown, 2026-12-01 Foundry Workflows retire, 2026-12-09 Azure gpt-4o 2024-05-13 retires.

flashcards.front: Why label every product fact with a date and a status?
flashcards.back: Vendors change names, defaults and availability within months. A fact without a date and a GA or preview label cannot be checked.

flashcards.front: What is a good study loop for one world?
flashcards.back: Read the brief, argue the dials aloud, take the quiz, write the defend answer from memory, then review the flashcards the next day.

glossary.def: A constraint you can change, such as scale, latency or permission model, that moves which option wins.
The five-move answer method: clarify the dials, list options, pick and flip, name failure modes, name metrics and rollout.
The dial and threshold at which your chosen option stops being the best one.
The simplest approach that could work. It is the baseline every other option must beat.
A named way a design breaks, with the symptom you would see and the signal you would use to detect it.
The last level of a world. It poses an interview-style question with unspecified dials and scores your answer against a rubric.
A dated list of changes with the source and status of each, used to check a fact before quoting it.
Generally available. The vendor supports the feature for production use under its normal terms.
Available for early use, usually without an SLA, and likely to change. Label it as preview in an answer.
The date a vendor stops serving an API or model. After it, calls fail, so plan the migration before the date.

claims.text: Anthropic says a knowledge base under about 200,000 tokens can go straight into the prompt.
OpenAI released the Responses API on 2025-03-11.
OpenAI released the Conversations API on 2025-08-20, and it is not ZDR eligible.
OpenAI announced the Assistants API deprecation on 2025-08-26 and sunset it on 2026-08-26.
From GPT-5.4 (2026-03-05), Chat Completions rejects tools when reasoning effort is not none.
Claude Opus 4.7 (2026-04-16) uses a new tokenizer that gives about 30% more tokens, adds xhigh effort and returns 400 for non-default sampling values.
GPT-6 Astra (2026-09-03) rejects reasoning.effort none with HTTP 400 and adds async tool calling.
From the GPT-5.6 family, cache writes bill at 1.25x the input rate, explicit breakpoints and prompt_cache_options appear, and prompt_cache_retention is deprecated.
Prompt Cache Diagnostics reached GA in the Responses API for GPT-5.6 and later on 2026-09-08.
On GPT-6, prompt_cache_retention is replaced by prompt_cache_options.ttl with the value 30m.
OpenAI's Evals platform is read-only from 2026-10-31 and shuts down on 2026-11-30, together with reusable prompts and Agent Builder.
OpenAI shuts down gpt-4, gpt-4-turbo, gpt-3.5-turbo, o1, o3-mini, o4-mini, gpt-4.1-nano and gpt-4o-2024-05-13 on 2026-10-23.
Azure retires o1, o1-pro, o3, o3-mini, o3-pro, o4-mini and o3-deep-research on 2026-11-19 and gpt-4o 2024-05-13 on 2026-12-09.
The Azure OpenAI v1 API uses a base URL ending /openai/v1 and needs no api-version.
The MCP revision dated 2026-07-28 is stateless: no initialize call, no session id, and server/discover is required.
In the MCP revision dated 2026-07-28, sampling, roots, logging and dynamic client registration are deprecated and Tasks moved to an extension.
A2A v1.0.0 was released on 2026-03-12.
A2A v1.0.1 (2026-05-28) says HTTP+JSON SHOULD use application/a2a+json.
Foundry serves A2A preview 0.3 when a request has no version header and no a2a-version query value.

Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 was announced on 2026-04-03 for .NET and Python, with graph workflows, orchestrations, declarative YAML and MCP stable and memory, DevUI and hosted agent integration in preview.
Microsoft Agent 365 is GA for the Commercial segment on a per user basis as of 2026-05-01.
Support for the initial-preview Foundry hosted agent backend ends on 2026-08-20.
Foundry Workflows (preview) retire on 2026-12-01.
A private Azure Container Registry for hosted agents is supported only for Foundry projects created after 2026-06-25.
Azure OpenAI On Your Data retires on 2026-10-14.
Under the EU AI Omnibus, Annex III high-risk rules apply from 2027-12-02 and Annex I rules from 2028-08-02.
Azure AI Search 2026-04-01 is the latest stable version, and knowledge sources are GA while ingestionPermissionOptions stays preview.
